statement: The verifier itself refuses to perform the Governance adoption review, extending the producer-bar/separation-of-duties chain a further step: a verifier acting as its own adoption reviewer would collapse two of the operating model's four distinct states (VERIFIED, ADOPTED) into a single actor's judgement, which §38 explicitly forbids.

anchor: this process is the CORRECTION-001 author of this estate ... it also holds no governed lane on this work item at all
statement: A second, independent refusal on the same Governance-adoption-review step (following the verifier's own refusal in S0351) shows a candidate barred on two grounds at once — a cross-work-item identity bar (correction author of a related work item) and total lane-absence on this work item — confirming the recurring common blocker is the missing role=governance lane.

anchor: the ONLY allowed write: REGISTER { session = own runtime identity, role = commissioned role } ↓ governed HANDOFF ↓ human START (G-3)
statement: AST-019's constrained contract: given current runtime identity, commissioned work item, commissioned role, a valid fresh-session declaration, passed eligibility/independence checks, and no existing conflicting assignment, the ONLY allowed write is REGISTER{session=own identity, role=commissioned role}, followed by governed HANDOFF and human START; it never writes CONTINUATION, never calls AST-018's appoint, and never writes the raw record directly.

type_signature.domain: (runtime identity, commissioned work item, commissioned role, fresh-session declaration=UNRESOLVED, eligibility, no conflict)

anchor: next-actor.result NEXT_ACTOR_REQUIRED → role field = the authoritative next role; require --requested-role === role, else MISMATCH → STOP (GO-08) ... HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED + empty session set → first-binding case ... WORK_ITEM_STOPPED → exit 65, honest Inv-E blocker; the capability NEVER writes CONTINUATION
statement: The commission-resolution table maps every AST-018 next-actor result to a specific AST-019 behaviour: an authoritative next role must match the requested role exactly; an empty-session-set HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED is treated as the first-binding case, requiring the role to be named in the recorded human act; a STOPPED work item always fails closed since the capability never writes CONTINUATION.

experiment.hypothesis: GO-01..GO-25 correctly enforce the constrained self-registration contract without weakening AST-015/016/017/018
experiment.setup: 25 named contract tests plus a full regression run
experiment.assumptions: AST-015 append is the sole legal writer
experiment.method: RED-then-GREEN TDD, source-inspection for write-path purity, regression re-run
experiment.result: 25/25 passed, 270 assertions; full WorkflowEngine suite 147/1577 green; four canonical assets byte-unchanged vs HEAD
experiment.interpretation: the capability is implemented and self-verified but not yet independently verified
experiment.conclusion: IMPLEMENTED — NOT VERIFIED, NOT ADOPTED, NOT AUTHORIZED

anchor: VERIFIED ⛔ — NOT VERIFIED independently. The GO-01..GO-25 GREEN is the engineering slice's self-verification; per R-34/EP-02 the producer never accepts its own work.
statement: The AMENDMENT-001 completion report reiterates the four-state separation specifically for AST-019, explicitly naming the next step as the very capability this slice builds: a fresh eligible governance session binds via AST-019 itself to perform the Governance adoption review.

anchor: AST-019 check (read-only) → NOT POSSIBLE — 'The work item is stopped. Only an explicit continuation recorded by governance or the human can reopen it — this capability never writes a continuation itself'
statement: Live behavior confirms AST-019's read-only check command correctly reports NOT POSSIBLE while the work item is STOPPED, honestly naming the human as next actor rather than attempting or implying any self-continuation.

anchor: the capability whose success criterion is verbatim this scenario: the human order 'Start the Governance adoption review of KOS-OPERATING-MODEL-001' must not produce 'no lane therefore refuse'
statement: The exact scenario that motivated AST-019's design (a human ordering the Governance adoption review with no pre-existing lane for the reviewer) is now the live case this appointment sets up — showing the newly built capability's success criterion applied to the concrete blocking case that produced it.

anchor: I would not accept the statement: 'The Governance Interpreter determines the correct meaning.' That would be dangerous. It should instead be: 'The Governance Interpreter evaluates candidate interpretations against applicable governance context and determines whether a candidate is admissible for the requested act.'
statement: An externally-proposed formulation claiming a Governance Interpreter 'determines the correct meaning' is rejected as dangerous and replaced with a narrower one: the interpreter only evaluates candidate interpretations for admissibility against governance context, never becoming semantic-identity authority.

anchor: AH-6 — Interpretation/Execution Separation: KnowledgeOS should separate deterministic expression recognition and candidate generation from contextual governance interpretation and from authoritative workflow execution; ambiguity must remain explicit across the boundary rather than being resolved implicitly by the execution mechanism.
statement: AH-6, a candidate architectural hypothesis derived from a Panini-grammar/compiler-theory analogy, is proposed but explicitly held as a hypothesis to be tested against OQ-5/Port Contract rather than immediately adopted into the architecture.

anchor: The HPA standing rule now explicitly says that development should inform the HPA when research is needed, but never initiate a research track autonomously. ... Therefore I would not reopen SNF research merely because this idea is interesting.
statement: Restates a standing HPA governance rule that development may inform but never autonomously initiate a research track, and applies it here to decline reopening the closed SNF research track merely because the Sanskrit-grammar analogy is compelling.

anchor: K1 — Identity ... Representation equality must never automatically become identity equality. This is one of the fundamental KnowledgeOS invariants.
statement: K1 (Identity), the first of eight proposed Kernel capacities, asserts as a fundamental invariant that two representations being equal must never automatically be treated as the same identity.

anchor: K7 — Constitutional Admissibility ... The Kernel must determine: Is this proposed state transition constitutionally admissible? Not: Is this statement true? And not: Does the LLM think this is correct?
statement: K7 (Constitutional Admissibility), framed as probably the most important capacity, distinguishes 'is this transition admissible' from both 'is this statement true' and 'does the LLM think this is correct' — the Kernel adjudicates admissibility, never truth or model opinion.

anchor: The Kernel should be incapable of doing things that belong to interpretation. ... Instead: 'Provider P submitted candidate meaning X.' Then: 'Evidence E supports candidate X.' Then: 'Given the current KnowledgeAggregate and constitutional rules, transition T is admissible.'
statement: A hard architectural 'capacity ceiling': the Kernel must be structurally incapable of stating what an expression means; it may only report that a provider submitted a candidate meaning, that evidence supports it, and whether the resulting transition is admissible.

anchor: ❌ Semantic Compiler ... ❌ LLM ... ❌ Natural-language parser ... ❌ Workflow engine ... ❌ Database ... ❌ UI / API
statement: Six explicit exclusions from Kernel authority: semantic compiler/SNF/FST components, any LLM, any natural-language parser, the workflow engine, the database, and the UI/API — all treated as replaceable interpretation providers or infrastructure/adapters, never Kernel responsibilities.

anchor: The Six Pillars You Must Preserve: Identity, Evidence, Context, Provenance, Contradiction, History

unknown_candidate.why_uncertain: restates a near-identical six-item list to the prior file's eight capacities under a different name ('pillars' vs 'K1..K8'); unclear whether this is the same underlying object refined or a distinct formalization by a different contributing voice

statement: A six-pillar formulation (Identity, Evidence, Context, Provenance, Contradiction, History) of the same 'constitutional knowledge engine' concept, each paired with a stated implementation implication (e.g. every entity has a stable immutable URI/hash; every assertion carries a pointer to its supporting evidence).

anchor: 1. PROPOSAL RECEIPT ... 2. CONSTITUTIONAL PRE-CHECK ... 3. STATE RETRIEVAL & BINDING ... 4. CONSTITUTIONAL RESOLUTION ... 5. TRANSITION EXECUTION (if RESOLVED) ... 6. POST-TRANSITION VERIFICATION
statement: A six-stage Kernel state machine is proposed (proposal receipt → constitutional pre-check → state retrieval/binding → constitutional resolution → transition execution → post-transition verification), culminating in an output of RESOLVED/AMBIGUOUS/MISMATCH/UNRESOLVED at the resolution stage.

anchor: Your kernel must be fail-closed ... Ambiguous intent → Return AMBIGUOUS, request clarification, do NOT execute ... The kernel never guesses, never approximates, and never executes an invalid transition.
statement: A six-row fail-closed failure-mode table maps each named failure (ambiguous intent, missing evidence, contradiction detected, unauthorized actor, invalid context, history violation) to a specific non-executing refusal outcome.

anchor: CONSTITUTION <name> version <semver> ... RULE <rule_name> [priority <number>]: ... CONTRADICTION_RULE <rule_name>: ... TRANSITION_RULE <rule_name>:
statement: A first-cut Constitutional DSL grammar is specified (CONSTITUTION/IMPORT/CONTEXT/ENTITY/EVIDENCE/RULE/CONTRADICTION_RULE/TRANSITION_RULE blocks), illustrated with a worked GovernanceConstitution v2.3.0 example including a WorkItem entity, Document/Observation evidence types, and rules for evidence sufficiency and lifecycle transitions.

anchor: Action Vocabulary ... START_REVIEW, START_ADOPTION_REVIEW, CONTINUE, STOP, ADOPT, REJECT, ... The parser uses regex + slot filling
statement: A closed intent vocabulary (14 named actions, 8 entity types, 6 relationship types) with a regex-based pattern-grammar for slot-filling intent parsing is proposed, explicitly framed as closed rather than general NLP.

anchor: base_weights: CONSTITUTIONAL: 1.0, CONSENSUS: 0.9, APPROVAL: 0.8, ... contradiction_resolution_threshold: 1.5 # If evidence A weight > evidence B weight * 1.5, A supersedes B
statement: A numeric evidence-weighting scheme assigns fixed base weights per evidence type (0.2-1.0), multiplicative modifiers for authority/provenance-depth/validity/recency, and a 1.5x threshold for one claim to supersede a contradicting one (20% band triggers reconciliation or escalation instead).

assumptions.statement: a numeric weight difference of 1.5x is the correct threshold for automatic supersession

anchor: The document currently conflates: KnowledgeOS Domain ... Application/Governance ... Interpretation mechanisms ... Kernel infrastructure ... The uploaded document puts almost all of these into 'Kernel.'
statement: The prior constitutional-knowledge-engine proposal (S0358/S0359) is diagnosed as conflating four distinct layers — the KnowledgeOS domain proper, Application/Governance orchestration, Interpretation mechanisms, and Kernel infrastructure — into a single overloaded 'Kernel' responsibility.

anchor: A judge does not normally: tokenize language, parse syntax, retrieve databases, persist state, execute infrastructure, manage workflow. Yet this proposal gives the Kernel all of those responsibilities.
statement: The 'proposal→facts→law→verdict→execution' judge metaphor is warned to be dangerous if taken literally, because a real judge does not tokenize, parse, persist, execute infrastructure, or manage workflow — those responsibilities must be separated out of the Kernel even though the adjudication metaphor itself remains useful.

anchor: An intent is what the human appears to mean. A command is an authorized request to change domain state. Those are fundamentally different concepts. ... only after governance evaluation should we get: AuthorizedCommand: StartAdoptionReview
statement: A DDD distinction is proposed between an Intent Candidate (what the human appears to mean, produced by Interpretation) and an Authorized Command (an authorized request to change domain state, produced only after Governance Evaluation) — refining the earlier pipeline from 'raw proposal→Intent AST→constitutional validation→execution' into an eight-stage pipeline ending in a Domain Event.

anchor: mechanism score ≠ evidence weight ≠ domain confidence ≠ authority ... The Kernel should not silently turn: 0.8 > 0.3 into: therefore truth / therefore authority. That is precisely the kind of semantic laundering the architecture has been trying to prevent.
statement: Numeric evidence weighting is flagged as the single most important technical problem in the prior proposal: it risks laundering mechanism-derived confidence scores into domain truth or authority, directly contradicting a prior ruling (OQ-5) that confidence is a domain-owned structured epistemic attribute rather than a mechanism score, and should not be adopted without strong domain justification.
missing: final ruling on whether any numeric evidence model is admissible

lineage_claims.quote: OQ-5 just explicitly established: Confidence is a domain-owned structured epistemic attribute, not a mechanism confidence score.

anchor: 'Priority rules' also need DDD scrutiny ... Why should 'identity' outrank 'history'? ... Who owns those priorities? ... DDD tells us to discover the meaning and ownership of the rule first. Only afterward should we decide how rules are represented.
statement: The proposed integer rule-priority ordering is challenged not on implementation grounds but on ownership grounds: before representing priorities as sortable integers, the domain question of who owns and justifies that ordering (constitutional law vs application policy vs evaluation strategy) must be answered first.

anchor: Is Kernel implementation history part of the KnowledgeOS domain? Probably not. ... KnowledgeOS history ≠ Kernel software history. ... Software versioning belongs to the engineering system. Knowledge state belongs to KnowledgeOS.
statement: The prior proposal's 'self-audit'/self-versioning idea (the Kernel versions its own code as knowledge state) is rejected: Kernel software-implementation history and KnowledgeOS domain knowledge-state history are distinct concepts that may be linked via provenance but must never be conflated.

anchor: I would reject that sequencing for now. Not because the technology is bad. Because it is implementation-first. ... Building a DSL before answering those questions risks making the DSL become the architecture. That would invert DDD.
statement: The prior proposal's five-phase implementation sequencing (Constitutional DSL → Intent Parser → Constitutional Resolver → Trust Layer → Execution Layer) is explicitly rejected as implementation-first; domain concepts (aggregate, invariant, governance rule, interpretation mechanism, command, evidence, authority, boundary) must be answered before any DSL is built, else the DSL becomes the architecture by default.

anchor: What is the smallest set of responsibilities that KnowledgeOS must own in order to preserve the truth, authority, provenance, epistemic state, and constitutional invariants of a knowledge-state transition? Not: 'What components should the Kernel have?'

unknown_candidate.why_uncertain: restates the general minimal-Kernel question from a much earlier batch (B0005) in a new, specifically-worded form; unclear whether this is the same open question carried forward or a freshly reformulated one

statement: The central open question the whole Kernel-brainstorming thread should keep in front of it is reframed from a components-first question ('what should the Kernel have') to a responsibilities-first question ('what is the smallest set of responsibilities KnowledgeOS must own'), on the premise that the Kernel boundary should emerge from answering the latter rather than being designed directly.

anchor: This is architectural conflation at scale. The proposal treats the Kernel as a 'god object' that owns nearly every important capability in the system. ... The core error is treating a useful architectural metaphor (the constitutional adjudicator) as a domain concept, then using it as a container for every responsibility that seemed important.
statement: A formal DDD critical review names the core methodological error in the prior Constitutional Kernel proposal: an architectural metaphor (constitutional adjudicator) was treated as a domain concept and then used as a container for every responsibility that seemed important, producing a 'god object.'

anchor: Conflation 1: Interpretation ≠ Adjudication ... Conflation 2: Evidence Evaluation ≠ Evidence Preservation ... Conflation 3: Constitutional Rules ≠ Rule Engine ... Conflation 4: Adjudication ≠ Execution ... Conflation 5: Self-Audit ≠ Domain Responsibility ... Conflation 6: History ≠ Provenance ≠ Audit Log
statement: Six named conflations are identified and separated: natural-language parsing is a mechanism not a domain concept; numeric evidence weighting is mechanism-confidence not epistemic confidence; the constitution is domain policy while the rule engine is infrastructure; determining admissibility and executing the transition are different responsibilities; self-audit of the Kernel's own software is an infrastructure concern, not a domain one; and domain history, provenance, audit log, and event sourcing are four separately-owned concepts collapsed into one.

anchor: Candidate Bounded Contexts: Expression Context, Interpretation Context, Governance Context, Knowledge Context, Workflow Context, Evidence Context, Audit Context
statement: Seven candidate bounded contexts are proposed with an ownership-by-concept table (KnowledgeAggregate/Identity/Provenance/Contradiction owned only by Knowledge Context; Meaning Candidate/Intent owned by Interpretation Context; Constitutional Rules owned by Governance Context; Command owned by Application Context), explicitly labelled CANDIDATE, not established architecture, pending validation against the existing KnowledgeOS/EKS landscape.

anchor: Falsification Table ... 1. Kernel should parse proposals → MOVE OUT ... 4. Kernel should weight evidence numerically → MOVE OUT ... 5. Kernel should resolve contradictions → SPLIT (detect in Kernel, resolve in Governance) ... 7. Kernel should own immutable history → KEEP (domain history only)
statement: A ten-row falsification table judges each claim from the prior Constitutional Kernel proposal as MOVE OUT (7 claims: parsing, candidate generation, semantic interpretation, numeric evidence weighting, execution, self-audit, GLR parsing), SPLIT (2 claims: contradiction resolution, constitutional DSL), or KEEP (1 claim, domain history only), yielding the restricted Kernel definition: identity, state-transition admissibility, history, provenance, contradiction detection, evidence-reference preservation.

anchor: 'Kernel = pure function' → HYPOTHESIS, not decision. ... A pure admissibility function and a domain aggregate are not necessarily the same thing.
statement: A subsequent challenge to the DDD critical review itself downgrades its conclusion that 'the Kernel is a pure function from (command, state, rules, evidence) to admissibility verdict' from an accepted decision to an open hypothesis, arguing the Kernel likely needs both a domain model (identity/state/provenance/contradiction/history/events) and a deterministic adjudication operation, not merely the latter.

lineage_claims.quote: I would not accept that wording yet.

anchor: adjudicate(state₁, command) → admissible ... something happens ... execute(state₂, command) ... The state could have changed between adjudication and application.
statement: Separating adjudication from execution too aggressively risks a transactional gap: the aggregate's state could change between the moment admissibility is determined and the moment the transition is actually applied, so who owns the actual state mutation (Kernel vs Application/Workflow) needs a stronger transactional answer than a simple 'Kernel says ADMISSIBLE, then Application executes' handoff.

anchor: if Governance simply sends an arbitrary rule set to the Kernel ... the Kernel is effectively saying: 'I will accept whatever someone calls the Constitution.' That isn't necessarily safe. ... 'The Kernel evaluates a transition against the authoritative constitutional policy applicable to that transition.'
statement: The critique's formulation 'the Kernel applies the rules as provided by the Governance Context' is challenged as unsafe because it implies the Kernel would accept whatever rule set is handed to it; the formulation is corrected to require the Kernel evaluate against the authoritative constitutional policy applicable to the transition, with source/certification/version/admissibility of that policy remaining governed.

anchor: DeepSeek invented some bounded contexts ... These are candidate contexts, not established architecture. ... DDD says: discover bounded contexts from domain boundaries and language; don't manufacture them from architectural neatness.
statement: The seven proposed bounded contexts (Expression/Interpretation/Governance/Knowledge/Workflow/Evidence/Audit) are flagged as the review's biggest methodological risk — invented from conceptual neatness rather than discovered from actual domain boundaries and existing ubiquitous language — and must be labelled CANDIDATE BOUNDED CONTEXTS pending validation.

anchor: Single admission gate MUST EXIST; Contract-conformance enforcement MUST EXIST; Identity assignment MUST EXIST; Evidence admission MUST EXIST; Justification preservation + sufficiency evaluation MUST EXIST; History recording MUST EXIST; Representation-agnostic intake MUST EXIST; Epistemic-state determination MUST EXIST; Confidence assignment inside boundary MUST EXIST
statement: Prior F-1..F-5 work is reported to have confirmed capabilities already present in existing law (not invented new ones), yielding a concrete 9-row MUST-EXIST domain capability map used to argue the Kernel-as-pure-admissibility-function formulation is too small — the domain already has authoritative responsibilities around identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation/sufficiency, epistemic-state determination, confidence, and history.

lineage_claims.quote: The F-1…F-5 evidence tells us that this formulation is too small.

anchor: The Kernel is probably not 'the constitutional validator' ... The Kernel is the authoritative admission boundary of KnowledgeCore. Its constitutional admissibility responsibility exists inside that boundary, but it is not the whole definition.
statement: The Kernel's identity is reframed a third time in this batch: not a god-Kernel, not merely DeepSeek's constitutional-validator/pure-function, but 'the authoritative admission boundary of KnowledgeCore,' inside which constitutional admissibility is one responsibility among identity assignment, epistemic state, evidence/justification/confidence, and history.

anchor: The KnowledgeCore accepts any representable submission. Natural language is therefore just one possible surface representation. The candidate shape is invariant; the surface representation isn't.
statement: F-3's result that KnowledgeCore accepts any representable submission gives the Sanskrit/FST/compiler research a clean architectural home outside the Kernel: natural language, structured data, and formal notation all reduce to the same canonical candidate shape before admission, validating the earlier candidate-set insight (AH-6) while explicitly removing it from the Kernel.

anchor: F-4 explicitly prohibits the tempting architecture: candidate → candidate database → Kernel later. Non-admitted candidates are not KnowledgeOS domain state. ... There is no hidden semantic aggregate.
statement: F-4 forbids a candidate-persistence architecture ('store candidates now, decide admissibility later'): a non-admitted candidate is never KnowledgeOS domain state — it is either recorded in History as part of an already-admitted transition, or lives entirely mechanism/infrastructure-side — a strong anti-god-Kernel constraint against a hidden semantic aggregate.

anchor: research_required: NO; research_track_opened: NO; kernel_designed: NO; kernel_implemented: NO; domain_model_changed: NO; aggregate_changed: NO; invariants_changed: NO ... So I would not ask DeepSeek for more research now.
statement: F-1..F-5's own concluding YAML block records that it opened no new research track, designed and implemented no Kernel, and changed no domain model/aggregate/invariants, explicitly returning control to the HPA; the reviewing voice concludes no further research round is warranted and proposes instead a single, code-free, thirteen-part DDD consolidation question as the final step before deciding what the Kernel actually is.

anchor: Single admission gate MUST EXIST; Contract-conformance enforcement MUST EXIST; Identity assignment MUST EXIST; Evidence admission MUST EXIST; Justification preservation + sufficiency evaluation MUST EXIST; History recording MUST EXIST; Representation-agnostic intake MUST EXIST; Epistemic-state determination MUST EXIST; Confidence assignment inside boundary MUST EXIST
statement: Verbatim restatement (in a separately-timestamped file) of the 9-row F-1..F-5 MUST-EXIST domain capability map and the conclusion that DeepSeek's Kernel-as-pure-function formulation is too small; content is identical to the corresponding section of S0361 and adds no new claim beyond it.

anchor: F-4 explicitly prohibits the tempting architecture: candidate → candidate database → Kernel later. Non-admitted candidates are not KnowledgeOS domain state.
statement: Duplicate restatement of F-4's anti-candidate-persistence constraint (no hidden semantic aggregate; non-admitted candidates are never domain state), identical in substance to the corresponding S0361 contribution.
